sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Southfield, Michigan?
sections.html:
Southfield now has a point-of-sale inspection requirement for residential homes, and it shapes how quickly a sale can close. The City Council approved the program in April 2026 under Ordinance 1835, so build the inspection into your timeline before you accept an offer.

Southfield is an inner-ring suburb of Detroit in Oakland County, with a population the Census Bureau puts at 76,111 for July 2025. Only 53.4 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, so a good share of the city's homes are rented.

Owners generally choose among three routes:

  • List with an agent and go through showings, a buyer's financing and the city inspection.
  • Sell directly to a buyer you find yourself and handle the paperwork with a title company.
  • Accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as-is, including any items the city inspection cites. Ask who will pay for those repairs before you agree.

sections.h2: How does the Southfield point-of-sale inspection work?
sections.html:
Southfield's Building and Safety Engineering department performs the inspection and issues a Certificate of Occupancy once violations are cleared. The city's Point of Sale packet explains the steps, and applications go through the BS&A online portal.

  • The packet lists a $190 resale inspection fee, made up of a $40 application fee, a $50 certificate of occupancy fee and $100 for the building trade, which includes one reinspection.
  • The fee must be paid in full before the inspection. A staff member then schedules it within 14 days of payment.
  • Someone must be at the house for the full inspection period, with morning slots from 9:30 to 12:30 and afternoon slots from 12:30 to 3:30.
  • The seller can fix the listed violations and call for a reinspection, which is included for selling homeowners.
  • Or the buyer can sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations with the seller before closing, and then has 30 days after closing to finish repairs.

The affidavit notes that a performance bond is required, with the amount depending on the extent of repairs, and that no one may occupy the house until violations are corrected and reinspected. Life safety items must be fixed before occupancy. Call the Building Department at 248-796-4100 with questions about your address.

sections.h2: What is Southfield like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Southfield sits about 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit and covers 26.25 square miles of land. Eight Mile Road forms the southern boundary, Inkster Road the western one and Greenfield Road the eastern one, and the northern edge runs roughly along Thirteen Mile Road. The separate city of Lathrup Village is an enclave inside Southfield's eastern part.

The area was surveyed in 1817 and organized as a township in 1830. Residents voted to incorporate as a city on April 28, 1958. Growth was fast after that: the 1960 census counted 31,531 people and the 1970 census counted 69,298. Wikipedia also describes the city as a historic center of mid-century modern architecture in Michigan.

The economy is built around offices. Wikipedia reports about 27 million square feet of office space and more than 100 Fortune 500 companies with offices in the city, along with several television stations and Lawrence Technological University. Northland Center, one of the first shopping malls in the country, opened in 1954 and closed in 2015, and its site has been under redevelopment as a mixed-use project.

sections.h2: How can I prepare a Southfield house for the inspection?
sections.html:
Ask the Building Department what the inspector will check at your address, and look for open permits from past work that never received a final sign-off. The city packet also includes a Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings, so have your mechanical system serviced by a contractor registered with the city.

Book the inspection early, since the 14-day scheduling window starts only after payment. Gather the documents a title company will ask for as well: the deed, your mortgage payoff figure and any permit records. If you plan to let the buyer assume the repairs, have the Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations ready so both sides sign before the closing table.

sections.html:
Southfield's numbers show a city with more renters than most Michigan suburbs and higher incomes than Saginaw or Southgate.

The 2020 census recorded 37,650 housing units in Southfield, 7.3 percent of them vacant. Persons aged 65 and older make up 22.6 percent of the population in the Census estimate.

Commute time averages 23.7 minutes for workers in the city, and 91.9 percent of households report a broadband subscription, two details that matter to buyers who work from home or drive to the Detroit area's job centers.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and districts shape a Southfield sale?
sections.html:
Southfield Public Schools operates the city's schools, and Southfield Senior High School for the Arts and Technology is the district's only high school since the two earlier high schools merged after the 2015-16 school year. Wikipedia also notes that students in parts of northern Southfield attend Birmingham schools and students in the southeast corner attend Oak Park schools. Confirm your own address with the district, because buyers ask.

Roads are a strength. The Lodge Freeway (M-10), I-696, the Southfield Freeway (M-39) and Telegraph Road (US-24) all pass through the city, and the Mixing Bowl interchange joins several of them near Lahser and Franklin roads. SMART buses serve local and regional routes. Major streets follow a mile grid, with 9, 10, 11 and 12 Mile Roads running east and west and Telegraph, Lahser, Evergreen and Greenfield running north and south.

Lawrence Technological University and Oakland Community College are both in the city.

sections.h2: What happens at recording in Oakland County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Southfield property are recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds in Pontiac. The office's recording page says a warranty deed, a deed containing a warranty clause and a land contract must be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office before they can be recorded.

The same page lists these eligibility basics for any deed:

  • Original signatures, with names typed or printed beneath them.
  • A notary acknowledgment for documents signed in Michigan.
  • The grantee's name and address on the face of the deed.
  • The total value of the property stated on the document or in an attached affidavit.
  • Black ink on white paper, with a 2.5 inch top margin on the first page.

The Register of Deeds can be reached at 248-858-0597. Ask the office for the current recording fee and the county transfer tax rate before the closing date. Michigan Treasury guidance sets a 45-day window for the buyer's Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, filed with the local assessor.

sections.h2: What if the Southfield house is vacant or a rental?
sections.html:
The Building Department's forms page lists a Rental Registration form, a Vacant Building Registration Application and separate vacant building owner and purchaser affidavits, so both situations have paperwork on file. Ask the Building Department which forms apply to your address before you list.

A tenant-occupied house adds timing to the point-of-sale process, since someone must be present for the inspection. A vacant house should be secured, heated through cold months and kept free of debris so an inspector sees the real condition.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Southfield?
faqs.a: Yes. Southfield City Council approved point-of-sale inspections for residential homes in April 2026 under Ordinance 1835. The packet lists a $190 resale inspection fee and a certificate of occupancy once violations are corrected.

faqs.q: Can the buyer take over the repairs the inspector lists?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller and buyer sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing. The buyer then has 30 days after closing to finish repairs and get a reinspection, and a performance bond is required.

faqs.q: How fast is the inspection scheduled in Southfield?
faqs.a: Staff schedule it within 14 days of the fee payment. Someone must be at the house for the whole window.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Southfield deed?
faqs.a: The Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed or land contract needs tax certification from the Oakland County Treasurer's Office first. The Register of Deeds phone number is 248-858-0597.

faqs.q: Will a cash sale skip the Southfield inspection?
faqs.a: No. The point-of-sale rules apply to residential sales in the city whatever the buyer's financing. A cash buyer can agree to assume the cited repairs through the affidavit, which can keep a closing moving.
